evals.prompt: Create `borrowing.em.hcl` for a library. A member uses a checkout screen to borrow an available book copy. Borrow Book produces Book Borrowed; reject an attempt when the copy is already on loan. Members can view their current loans. When a loan becomes overdue, the system should request an overdue notice without human input. Include UUID member_id and copy_id contracts, concrete Read Model questions, and scenarios. Write the file in the current directory and validate it if the Event Modeling HCL CLI is available.
evals.expected_output: A coherent valid v0.7.0 model with one board in business-time order, containing State Change, State View, and Automation workflows with owned Events, reusable field types, explicit field types, canonical flows, and pattern-correct scenarios.
expectations: Because the request creates an Event Model from domain prose, business meaning is established with the event-modeling skill before event-modeling-hcl encodes it. The HCL skill is not used as a substitute for business discovery.

The output is a `.em.hcl` file with lower-snake-case block labels, context-owned Events, one `board` block that lists every workflow in business-time order, and an explicit `type` on every field and subfield.
Borrowing is a state_change with Screen to Command and Command to Event expressed in canonical direction.
Current loans is a state_view whose Read Model has a concrete question and whose scenario has Given Event and Then Read Model with no When step.
The overdue notice reaction is an automation consuming only internal Events, with a pending-work read model feeding the processor, and includes a machine-action scenario using HCL When/Then grammar.
member_id and copy_id are reusable UUID field types and connected contract fields pass an information-provenance review without a mapping DSL.
The already-on-loan rule appears as an observable error scenario rather than invented implementation logic or expect_empty_list.

evals.prompt: From this requirement, create `payment-activation.em.hcl`: Stripe sends Payment Captured. Our Subscriptions domain uses that fact to Activate Subscription and records Subscription Activated. The payment message contains payment_id, subscription_id, amount, and currency. We do not yet know whether partial payments activate a subscription. Model that uncertainty rather than choosing a rule. Include a success scenario and validate the model if possible.
evals.expected_output: An automation workflow that translates an external Stripe-owned Event into an internal Subscription Event, preserving the partial-payment question as an attached open hotspot.
expectations: The event-modeling skill establishes business meaning and missing decisions before event-modeling-hcl encodes the model; legal syntax is not treated as evidence that the unknown activation rule is decided.
Stripe is represented by an external system and an external bounded context that owns Payment Captured.

The workflow is an `automation` (no `translation` keyword exists) that consumes the external Event through canonical from flow, preferably via a pending-work read model, so tools derive it as a translation.
The internal Command and Event use Subscriptions domain language and are connected in canonical direction. The internal event is not a linked copy of the Stripe event.
payment_id, subscription_id, amount, and currency are represented with reusable typed contracts and traceable flow. No mapping, linked_copy, or storyline attribute is introduced.
A pattern-correct success scenario is present: Given the external event, When the processor or command, Then the internal event.
The partial-payment uncertainty is an open hotspot attached to a relevant workflow or element; no activation rule is fabricated.

evals.prompt: Review and replace the following idea with a valid `order-status.em.hcl` model: 'Create a query command called GetOrderStatus. It reads OrderPlaced, OrderShipped, and OrderDelivered and returns OrderStatusDto. The screen points backward to the DTO.' Model what an authenticated customer needs to see, include order_id and status fields, and add scenarios for placed and delivered orders. Keep the business behavior but correct Event Modeling and HCL mistakes. Validate if tooling is available.
evals.expected_output: A State View model with catalog Events, a question-driven Read Model, canonical Event-to-Read-Model-to-Screen flow, and Given/Then scenarios without a fake query Command.
expectations: The business review uses event-modeling, then event-modeling-hcl encodes the corrected model. This explicit review-and-replace request permits changes, unlike a review-only request.
The model contains no Query concept, fake GetOrderStatus Command, query attribute, or storyline block.
OrderPlaced, OrderShipped, and OrderDelivered are past-tense Events owned by a bounded context, each declared once.
The State View Read Model asks one concrete order-status question and consumes Events using from.
The Read Model points to the Screen with to; the Screen does not point backward with from and does not issue multiple commands.
Both scenarios use Given Event then Read Model and contain no When step.
order_id and status have valid field typing and their Read Model provenance is visible without a mapping attribute.

evals.prompt: Update `locked-order.em.hcl`. It has state_change "place_order" with status = "done" and a created state_view "view_order". Add the supplied loyalty_id field to the view only; event.orders.order_placed already supplies it as field_type.orders.loyalty_id. Do not reopen completed work. The place-order screen currently issues both place_order and apply_coupon; leave that screen locked, but say what is wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: The created state view gains loyalty_id from the existing Order Placed event. The done state_change and shared catalog contracts are unchanged. The reply names the bed on the locked screen without editing it.
expectations: The done workflow is not modified and its status is not changed.

The created state view is updated with loyalty_id typed as field_type.orders.loyalty_id and sourced through event.orders.order_placed. Existing catalog contracts need no changes and remain unchanged; no mapping DSL, linked_copy, or storyline attribute is added.
The reply identifies the locked screen's two commands as a bed, meaning any second command, and does not silently split that locked workflow.
No implementation code is generated.

evals.prompt: Split the supplied `clinic.em.hcl` into a folder model `clinic/` so that each team can own its own workflows. It contains a clinic bounded context, receptionist actor, register_pet, pet_directory, and notify_owner workflows, their chapter, and an open hotspot on the notify_owner processor. Keep the board order, chapter membership, ownership, scenarios, and the unanswered notice-timing question unchanged. Format and validate the folder if a compatible CLI is available.
evals.expected_output: A folder of member `.em.hcl` files with the same business model and single board, validated as one folder model with no EM014, EM015, or EM016 diagnostic. The open hotspot remains a workshop uncertainty.
expectations: Every block moves whole into a file directly in `clinic/`. No block spans two files, and no `include` or `import` block is invented.
The bounded context with all its events, aggregates, and field types is in one file.
The single `board` block moves whole into one file and keeps its workflow list unchanged, so the story order is the same. The chapter keeps its membership; no workflow is in two chapters.
File names may use a prefix for human reading order, but the reply does not rely on file order for the board. No ID is declared twice across files.

With emhcl v0.16.0 or newer, the folder is formatted with `emhcl fmt -w clinic` or by formatting each member file, and validated with `emhcl validate clinic`. The agent does not falsely claim current fmt refuses folders, validate members separately as complete models, or claim an older CLI verifies v0.7.0.

The owner_notice_timing hotspot stays open and attached to processor.notify_owner.owner_notifier, with its original question. No timing rule is invented, the reply does not call the model implementation-ready, and any strict EM406 failure is reported rather than suppressed.

evals.prompt: The supplied `legacy.em.hcl` is a v0.4.0 model: it has no board, typeless order_id and partner_order_id fields backed by uniquely named field types, and translation "import_partner_order". Bring it to the current language without changing its meaning and validate it if the CLI is available. Preserve meaningful existing titles such as Customer purchases and Checkout purchase; do not leave redundant titles that merely spell out an ID.
evals.expected_output: The model is converted with `emhcl migrate -w legacy.em.hcl`, its migration report is read, redundant ID-derived titles are removed, meaningful titles are preserved, and the observed validation result is reported.
expectations: When a compatible CLI is available, the agent uses `emhcl migrate -w legacy.em.hcl` and reads its report rather than hand-converting v0.4.0 constructs. A non-writing preview is allowed but not required. Without the CLI, the limitation is explicit and no executed migration or validation is claimed.

The result has one board listing place_order, view_order, and import_partner_order in their former order, explicit qualified field_type.orders.order_id or field_type.partner.partner_order_id types on every formerly typeless field, and automation in place of translation.

Customer purchases and Checkout purchase remain as meaningful titles. Migration-generated titles that merely repeat an ID's words, such as Order Placed, View Order, and Import Partner Order, are removed; no blanket keep-all or delete-all title policy is used.
The migrated model is formatted and validated with emhcl validate legacy.em.hcl when compatible tooling is available, and the observed migration report and command results are reported.

evals.prompt: Repair only the HCL language errors in `syntax-repair.em.hcl`: the place_order command's to target must be the unquoted event.orders.order_placed traversal, and its order_id field must explicitly use field_type.orders.order_id. The business facts, workflow boundary, labels, board order, and scenario are settled; do not run a business discovery or redesign. Format and validate with compatible tooling if available.
evals.expected_output: A narrow HCL repair that preserves the existing business model and reports only commands actually run.
expectations: The command's to edge becomes the unquoted event.orders.order_placed traversal and its order_id field gains type = field_type.orders.order_id.
The original workflow, screen issuer, event, actor, board order, description, and scenario behavior remain unchanged; no new business rules, fields, slices, or speculative scenarios are added.

The HCL skill handles the syntax-only request without invoking a business workshop or loading the business methodology merely to perform the two explicit repairs. The shared edit policy may still be consulted.
Formatting and normal validation are attempted only with compatible emhcl. Any unavailable tooling is stated honestly; the reply does not claim validation from inspection.
No implementation code or source-string assertion tests are created.

evals.prompt: In `shared-contract.em.hcl`, change the shared field_type.orders.order_id from UUID to String so checkout can submit order references such as WEB-42. I confirm this change for place_order only. Do not edit view_order, which is in review. Check whether you can safely apply the shared contract change under those limits; do not create a separate shadow contract or split the model to get around them.
evals.expected_output: The change is blocked as a whole because the shared field type also changes the locked view_order contract even if its workflow block is not textually edited. The existing file remains unchanged and the reply names the missing authorization.
expectations: The agent traces field_type.orders.order_id through the canonical order_placed event into the review-status view_order read model and its scenarios, rather than inspecting only workflow-local text edits.
The shared field type, event, created producer, locked consumer, examples, board, and statuses remain unchanged. No partial producer edit is made while the linked consumer is locked.

The reply identifies view_order as locked, explains that changing the shared type indirectly changes its contract, and requests confirmation naming view_order and this UUID-to-String change before applying the chain edit.
Confirmation naming place_order alone does not unlock view_order. No cloned field type, alternate event, bypass workflow, status downgrade, or other workaround evades the lock.
No successful repair, formatting, or validation command is claimed unless it was actually executed; no production implementation code is added.
